_comment: The yardstick. One entry per capture in ../captures/manifest.json, and every facet a capture is scored on is named EXPLICITLY here — there is no aggregate number and no facet a reader has to infer. A facet a capture's entry does not name is not scored for that capture and does not enter that facet's denominator.

_facets.status: the terminal queue status: filed | rejected | failed. Every capture reaches one of them in a SINGLE phase — a capture never waits on a person, so there is no state here that is not terminal.
_facets.reason: for a `rejected` status, the report's own reason_code (capture.schema.REJECTION_REASONS)
_facets.type: the `type:` frontmatter of the page that actually landed, read back out of git
_facets.folder: the directory the page landed in
_facets.anchor: {kind: entity|company, ids: [registry id, ...]} — read from the filed page's server-stamped `entity:` frontmatter, so it is the resolved REGISTRY ID and never the agent's spelling. `company` means the page filed with an empty `entity:` list, which is what a company-wide anchoring outcome stamps.
_facets.attempts: how many times the agent was called for this capture (counted at the Deps.agent seam, not read from any report)
_facets.bounces: corrective retries = max(0, attempts - 1); one bounce means the first pass was vetoed and the agent got its single corrective pass
_facets.proposals: for a capture naming something the registry does not know: the identity the filing PROPOSED for it, by NAME and matched loosely (run_filing._proposals_match). The librarian creates the entity page itself with `approved_by:` empty, regenerates the registry and anchors the capture to it in the same commit, so what this scores is WHICH unregistered thing was given an identity — never the spelling the agent chose for it, and never the id, which is slugify(name) and would score that spelling. Extras do not fail the facet: a second proposal beside the expected one is already fenced by librarian.identity's three honesty checks (named in the material, no collision with a registered spelling, not a name a steward has declined).
_facets.pages: the page SET one capture established — `report['pages_filed']`, one entry per page, paired one-to-one and greedily in the order written. An entry asserts its own ANCHOR (exact — a resolved registry id, or the empty list a company-wide outcome stamps) and MAY assert a title (matched loosely — see the runner and _morphology). RENAMED from `decisions` when the meeting flow was folded into the one pipe: that facet counted the `decision` pages a meeting flow wrote into `wiki/decisions/`, and there is no `decision` type and no meeting flow left. The PROPERTY is unchanged, and it is the one a single-anchor implementation cannot express — a transcript that establishes two conclusions owes two pages, each anchored on its own aboutness — so the count is load-bearing in BOTH directions: one page where two were expected is two conclusions lumped together, and five is a granularity failure rather than over-delivery. The anchor is the load-bearing pair-er and the title is optional because that is what five measured runs of the retired flow showed over these same two transcripts: across three distinct brittleness shapes the anchors were right every time while the titles were stable only in a proper noun or a term the transcript itself repeats. So a title is written where it HELD and omitted where a defensible paraphrase could put the word on the sibling page — omitting it moves the assertion off the model's vocabulary and onto its judgment, which is what this facet is for. An entry asserting neither is refused by _check_set (it would match whatever page is left), and a title-less entry must be written LAST because it is the weakest matcher. The verbatim `sources/` archive is deliberately NOT in `pages_filed`, so it is never among the pages counted here — it is the captured material, not something the capture established.

_looseness: Titles are matched on normalized words, never literally: an expected title matches a page when every significant word of the expectation appears in the page's own path, in either grammatical number (see _morphology). evals/README.md records what a literal-word expectation cost the QA golden (`globex-meeting-budget`); this set does not repeat it. Everything else — status, ids, folders, counts — is exact, because those are facts with one spelling.
_morphology: An expected title is written in UNINFLECTED content words — a proper noun plus a stable noun — and never in the verb form one run happened to produce. run_filing._words does no stemming and deliberately will not grow any (a stem table is a second yardstick nobody reviews), so `tracked` and `tracking` are still two different words and an expectation naming one of them scores the model's grammar. EXACTLY ONE fold is made, at the comparison rather than in the tokenizer (run_filing._same_word): a trailing `s`, in either direction, so `review` and `reviews` are one word. It was added on MEASUREMENT, not on taste — three independent runs of the same code on the same model titled F08's review conclusion two ways, singular twice (PASS) and plural once (FAIL), with the anchors right every time, so a 2-denominator facet was flipping on grammatical number. That expectation no longer names a title at all (F08's second entry pairs on its anchor alone since the one pipe landed), so the fold is currently unexercised by the shipped set and is kept rather than reverted: it is strictly weaker than the predicate it replaced, it cost a measured FAIL to discover, and the next title written here inherits it. A plural written `es` is still not folded (`process`/`processes` misses), which is the measure of how narrow this is. The fold is ONE-DIRECTIONAL — the predicate is strictly weaker than the one it replaces, so a recorded PASS cannot become a FAIL and only a FAIL can flip; that is what keeps every score already in evals/history.ndjson comparable without a re-run. Where two expected pages could both match one page, the MORE SPECIFIC one is written first: matching is greedy and one-to-one, so the narrow expectation has to claim its page before the broad one takes it — and that pairing is the one place a weaker predicate could still re-bind and cost a PASS, which is why tests/evals/test_filing_golden_fixture.py::test_no_expected_page_title_can_swallow_a_later_ones_page calls the same matcher and so widened its own net with it.
_fixture_narration: These expectations, and PROVENANCE.json beside the mini repo, are where the reasoning about the MEASUREMENT lives — never in the fixture pages themselves. The agent under measurement reads those pages while it files, so a page explaining which facet it exists to probe is a page telling the model the answer, and a score measured that way is not a score. The pages read as ordinary knowledge a colleague wrote; every `why` below says what that page is doing for the instrument.

expectations.why: The base case: ordinary prose about a registered entity, filed as a note. If this one moves, nothing else in the set is interpretable.

A capture about an organization the registry does not know used to PARK and ask its submitter, and this entry used to be two phases with a stored reply between them. the file-first write path retired that: the librarian creates `wiki/entities/Halcyon Grid.md` with `approved_by:` empty, regenerates the registry and anchors the note to it in the SAME commit, and a steward confirms the identity afterwards from the inbox. So the capture files in one phase, and what it is scored on is whether the unregistered thing got an identity at all. The two shortcuts it must not take are unchanged and both leave `proposals` empty: anchoring to whichever registered organization the corpus talks about most, or falling back to company-wide scope. It names NO `anchor` expectation, and that silence is deliberate rather than an omission — a proposal's id is `slugify` of the name the AGENT chose, so pinning `halcyon-grid` would score one defensible spelling of a judgment `proposals` already scores through the loose matcher, and score it twice. It names no `attempts`/`bounces` either: each of the three honesty checks in `librarian.identity` answers with a Finding the corrective pass can act on, so a proposal may legitimately spend the second pass an ordinary filing does not.

The material answers the weekend-cover question `wiki/notes/Northwind Freight Onboarding.md` left open, and substantially covers ground that page already covers — a backend that files a second page and says nothing about the first has quietly duplicated the corpus. RETIRED FACET: this entry used to pin the reciprocal `related:` link the filing declared on that page and code performed. A capture no longer declares an additive edit at all, so there is nothing mechanical left to score here; what the capture still owes is the page it files, and `status`/`type`/`folder`/`anchor` score that.

Byte-identical material to F01 from a different person: already in the graph, so it is refused with a pointer rather than filed a second time. Deterministic and pre-agent — this facet is the one that must NOT move between backends, and a change here means the dedup levels moved, not the model.

A conclusion that genuinely belongs to no entity. The failure this watches for is the tempting one: anchoring it to whichever organization the corpus talks about most, because an anchored page files and a company-wide one needs a written reason.

MOVED when the meeting flow was folded into the one pipe, and only the placement facets moved. This used to expect `type: decision` in `wiki/decisions/`; a conclusion is a `note` now — splitting conclusions into two folders by their grammatical mood bought nothing and forced a placement question at every filing — so `decision` is a type no flow can create and the two placement facets take the note vocabulary. The facet this capture exists for, `anchor`, does not move at all, which is why its cell stays comparable with every row already in evals/history.ndjson while `type` and `folder` do not. The capture ID keeps its old spelling on purpose: every recorded row and every evals/out/*.json names it, and renaming it would make those observations point at a capture nobody can find.
Material whose subject is a term rather than an event — the third creatable type, and the one a backend under pressure downgrades to a note.

Sixteen figures in one capture, one of them explicitly provisional. No gate re-checks figures at filing time, so what this scores is the surrounding judgment — right entity, right type, filed in one pass rather than bounced. It anchors to the entity every other capture ignores, which keeps its anchoring judgment independent of the one the corpus talks about most; and no page in the mini repo carries a figure of its own, so a number that appears on the filed page can only have come from this capture.

A transcript that settles TWO things, one of which belongs to an entity and the other to nobody — the property a single-anchor implementation cannot express and a single-conclusion transcript cannot reveal.

REWRITTEN when the meeting flow was folded into the one pipe. It used to expect the meeting flow's own page SET: `type: meeting` in `wiki/meetings/` with one `decision` page per decision beside it. Neither type exists — a meeting is an EVENT, so its transcript is archived verbatim under `sources/meetings/` and what it ESTABLISHED is filed as ordinary pages — so the placement facets score the first page the account declared (a `note` in `wiki/notes/`) and the whole set is scored by `pages`. Nothing about what this capture measures moved: two conclusions, two pages, each anchored on its own aboutness.

The two entries pair differently ON PURPOSE. The Northwind one keeps its title because `Northwind second wave` is a proper noun the transcript repeats and it held across every recorded run; the shared-review one drops its title and pairs on its ANCHOR alone. That title used to be the single word `review`, and the transcript decides 'one shared list of what every review has to cover', so `checklist` (the thing being REPLACED, named once in passing), `shared`, `scope` and `standardise` are each one plausible paraphrase away from absent — and the word that survived three runs survived them under a brief that no longer exists. The anchors carry the discrimination here anyway: this conclusion is the company-wide one and its sibling is not, so the pairing stays exact with no vocabulary in it. Title-less entry written LAST, which is what `_check_set` requires and what stops the weakest matcher taking its titled sibling's page.

It asserts no `anchor` of its own: that facet reads the FIRST declared page, and which of two equally correct conclusions an account puts first is not a judgment this set has ever scored.

The transcript half of F02, and the capture that has changed most often. A transcript whose subject is not in the registry used to park the WHOLE set in one ask, then re-file after a reply; the file-first write path removed the round trip, and the one pipe then removed the second flow. It files exactly like a typed note: the pages the transcript established land in one commit with `Project Wren` created as a proposed identity beside them, and the transcript itself is archived verbatim under `sources/meetings/`. The transcript states the problem out loud — 'nothing in our records knows what Project Wren is' — and then decides to write the conclusions down anyway, so a backend that treats the unknown name as a reason to stop has re-invented the park against a transcript that argued with it.

REWRITTEN with F08 when the meeting flow went: `type: meeting` in `wiki/meetings/` is a page no flow can create, so the placement facets score the first declared page (a `note` in `wiki/notes/`) and the set is scored by `pages`.

The two conclusions are 'Wren gets tracked formally' and 'the weekly summary joins the shared one', and they are paired on TITLE alone. There is no anchor to assert on either: each anchors to the proposed identity — whose id is slugify of the name the AGENT chose — or company-wide, and pinning either would pin the yardstick to one sample. WHICH title to assert was settled by re-scoring all SEVEN recorded runs of the old re-filed phase rather than by reading the newest one: `shared`, `summary` and `weekly` land on the summary conclusion in 7/7 and on the tracking conclusion in none, and `project wren` lands on the tracking conclusion in 7/7. So entry one asserts the bare word `summary` and entry two asserts `Wren`. `summary` is written FIRST because it is the narrow one — `Wren` appears in BOTH titles in six of the seven runs, so it is the broad matcher and the specific-first rule puts it second.

Those seven runs were measured under a brief and a flow that no longer exist, and the words are the TRANSCRIPT's own rather than that brief's, which is why they are kept rather than dropped. A red cell here on the first one-pipe run is a candidate for re-derivation from that run's own observed set, not a verdict on the backend.

The sharpest anchoring probe in the set. The material names two registered entities and is plainly about only one of them; the other appears in a single sentence that says so explicitly. A backend that anchors on mention frequency, on first mention, or on whichever entity the corpus knows best gets this wrong — and gets everything else in this set right, which is exactly the gradual degradation the instrument exists to catch.

The first of four captures added for issue #77, where entity resolution stopped being a suffix list in Python and became the agent's judgment fenced by code. This one is the case the suffix list NEVER had: the material consistently writes a group form of a registered name that `normalize` does not fold and never did, so no deterministic path resolves it in either direction. What DOES reach the agent is the registered entity itself, because whole-token containment already surfaces it — the material's token run carries the registered spelling inside it. So this measures judgment with the candidate already in hand: does the agent read a qualifier as the same company, and does it say so. Substantively unambiguous on purpose (depots, site access, a standing maintenance contract — the entity page's own subject matter), because an instrument whose fixture is genuinely ambiguous measures the ambiguity.

The ABBREVIATION direction, and the only case in the set that no wording in any skill could have fixed. The material writes the short house form and never the registered one, so whole-token containment of the REGISTRY spelling inside the material finds nothing: before `gather._entities` learned to match a distinctive sub-run of a registered name, this candidate never reached the agent at all and the capture could only park. The corpus evidence is on the entity's own page, phrased as the ordinary fact it is — nearly nobody writes the full name — exactly as the research partner's page has always recorded its own short form. Two things are being measured together here, which is deliberate: that the near miss is SURFACED (platform) and that it is JUDGED rather than guessed (agent).

The benign twin, and it matters MORE now that resolution is a judgment: the failure mode of an agentic resolver is a confident wrong answer, so this belongs here and not only in a unit test. Two registered entities share a prefix and are genuinely different organizations — an independent legal practice and a maintenance contractor, no ownership, no shared work — and BOTH are handed to the agent, because the material's token run carries the shorter registered name inside the longer one. The capture is about the practice alone and must anchor to it alone. A run that anchors this to the contractor, or to both, has merged two identities, and every page filed against the wrong one is a timeline nobody will re-read. The distinctness is written on both entity pages as ordinary knowledge — a real brain would hold exactly that fact, because a real brain's people confuse the two names too.

The regression guard for the judgment that MOVED. `Registry.canonical_id` used to fold a legal-form suffix, so this spelling resolved mechanically; it no longer does (`kernel.normalize` splits the resolution key from the mint gate's collision key), and the point of this capture is that the OUTCOME must not change even though the decider did. If moving judgment out of code lost behaviour, this is the cell that goes red, and it goes red for the whole class rather than for one spelling. Written as an ordinary operational note about a name mismatch on a certificate, not as a puzzle about names: the material's own subject happens to be the same confusion the resolver is being asked to see through, which is how the confusion actually shows up in a real brain.
